audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated ability names and one fabricated passive. spikes[1].text calls her W 'Stalking Shadows'; spikes[2].text, early and wants.foe[1] call her E 'Nightfall' and describe it as a STUN. early and spikes[0].text describe Spirit Abjuration as 'a personal shield' and a 'true-damage proc'.
audit.why: Aurora's W is Across the Veil (22/21/20/19/18s): a leap that makes her invisible and speeds her up. Her E is The Weirding (15/14/13/12/11s): a blast that damages and SLOWS, then hops her backward — there is no stun in it, so 'don't walk into her E stun' teaches the wrong fear. Spirit Abjuration exorcises spirits that follow her and HEAL her; it neither shields nor deals true damage.
audit.corrected: Real names and real effects used throughout: Across the Veil's invisible leap, The Weirding's slow-and-hop-back, Spirit Abjuration as sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagreed with the already-audited mirror at three of seven stages, and the packet flags it as contradicting the win rate: Yorick wins 52.27% but the chart handed Aurora five stages and Yorick none.
audit.why: The mirror audit (aurora__yorick) set the chart as one atomic group to Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Skill / Yorick with ratings 5/7/7/7/7/5/3 from Aurora's side. Restated from Yorick's side that is the same chart with ratings 5/3/3/3/3/5/7. It also resolves the win-rate defect by giving the 2-item side lane back to Yorick, which is where his 52.27% actually comes from.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3 and 6 flipped and all seven ratings brought into line, proposed as one atomic pair-matched group. whys[0], whys[2], whys[6], spikes[0].text, spikes[3].text, mid and late rewritten so the prose stops calling level 3 'the even beat' and stops calling late Aurora's.

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike carried a cooldown, so 'trade around her cooldown' had no number behind it anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Twofold Hex is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s, The Weirding 15/14/13/12/11s, Across the Veil 22/21/20/19/18s and Between Worlds 140/120/100s. Across the Veil at 22s against your Dark Procession at 20s is the trading window that decides the lane.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] carries Q's 9s, spikes[1] R's 140s and W's 22s, spikes[2] E's 15s, mid Mourning Mist's 12s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page told you to buy Grievous Wounds, and the reason was hidden behind the false 'shield' description of her passive.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule 'needs-antiheal': Spirit Abjuration heals her off the spirits her spells and attacks exorcise, so she out-sustains ghoul chip in exactly the extended trades Yorick wants.
audit.corrected: early now ends on bringing Grievous Wounds early, with the heal named as the reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text claimed 'her R zone where her damage amp stacks'.
audit.why: Riot's description of Between Worlds lists damage, a slow, and an area she can teleport across. There is no damage amplification in the text, and I could not verify one.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the slow, which is what the description actually supports. Recorded in unverified rather than asserted either way.

edits.before: Aurora wins level 1 — ranged Q and passive shield beat your point-blank trade.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — her ranged Q pokes, but Last Rites heals the chip back.

edits.before: Level 3 evens as ghouls block her Q and you can E-mist a real trade.
edits.after: Aurora holds 3 — The Weirding slows then hops her out of your reach.

edits.before: Aurora stays ahead at 2+ items as the superior pick-and-teamfight threat.
edits.after: Yorick takes 2+ items — Maiden and ghouls out-duel her in the side lane.

edits.before: Aurora controls the early lane — her Q Twofold Hex pokes from range and her passive Spirit Abjuration procs true damage plus a personal shield that eats your Last Rites trade. Level 3 is the even beat: use ghouls to block her Q line and E-mist her when she steps up to farm.
edits.after: Aurora controls the early lane — Twofold Hex (9s) pokes from range and Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spirit she exorcises, out-sustaining your chip. She keeps level 3 as well: The Weirding slows you and hops her back before your Mourning Mist matters.

edits.before: Aurora spikes at 6 — Between Worlds is a zone ult and her W Stalking Shadows gives an invisibility dash to reposition out of your Maiden. Hold W Cage to trap her W blink and don't fight inside her R zone where her damage amp stacks.
edits.after: Aurora spikes at 6 — Between Worlds (140s) leaves a slowing zone she can teleport across, and Across the Veil (22s) leaps her invisible out of your Maiden. Cage where she lands, and never fight inside the zone where its slow holds you.

edits.before: First-item favours Aurora: a mage mythic lets her burst you through your sustain before ghouls stack, and her E Nightfall stun sets up her whole combo. Build early MR and farm behind minions.
edits.after: First-item favours Aurora: a mage item bursts you through your sustain before ghouls stack, and The Weirding (15s) slows you into the rest of her combo. Build early MR and farm behind minions.

edits.before: The lock stays Aurora but late is your macro window — she wants teamfights and picks, you split-push. Shove with Maiden, take side towers when she rotates, and only 1v1 her with Cage ready to trap the W dash.
edits.after: Two items in, the side lane is yours — she wants teamfights and picks, you split-push. Shove with Maiden, take towers when she rotates, and duel her with Dark Procession ready to wall the Across the Veil escape.

edits.before: Aurora runs levels 1-2 — her Q Twofold Hex out-ranges your melee trade and her passive shield plus true-damage proc punish any step-up. Soak XP behind ghouls, block her Q with the wave, and don't walk into her E Nightfall stun.
edits.after: Aurora runs the early lane — Twofold Hex out-ranges your melee trade and Spirit Abjuration heals her back off every spell she lands. Soak XP behind ghouls, block her Q with the wave, and bring Grievous Wounds early.

edits.before: Level 3 is your even beat — use ghouls to eat her poke, then E Mourning Mist and Q when she comes to farm. She reasserts by 4, and at 6 Between Worlds plus her W invisibility dash make her all-in and escape strong, so save Cage for the W.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 stay hers — use ghouls to eat her poke and only Mourning Mist (12s) her once The Weirding is spent. At 6 Between Worlds (140s) plus Across the Veil's invisible leap make her all-in and escape strong, so cage her landing spot.

edits.before: Aurora favours the pick-and-teamfight game, so beat her on the map: split-push with Maiden, punish her rotations by taking towers, and only take a sidelane duel with W Cage up to trap her dash out.
edits.after: Once you have two items the side lane is yours: split-push with Maiden, punish her rotations by taking towers, and duel her with Dark Procession up to wall the Across the Veil escape.

edits.before: W Cage to trap her W blink or E stun setup
edits.after: Cage her landing spot, not her E slow line

edits.before: Q Twofold Hex poke behind passive shield
edits.after: Twofold Hex poke, Spirit Abjuration heals

edits.before: E Nightfall stun into full combo
edits.after: The Weirding's slow into full combo

notes: The chart follows the mirror (aurora__yorick), which had already been audited and set as an atomic group, so the two directions now agree without mirror-fix.js having to correct anything. Adopting it meant rewriting the prose that called level 3 'the even beat' and late 'Aurora's' — those seven prose edits are part of the same change and should land with the chart. UNVERIFIED, left out of the page: whether Between Worlds amplifies damage inside its zone (the old spikes[1] asserted it; Riot's text lists only damage, slow and traversal) and whether Across the Veil's invisibility makes Mist Walkers drop her the way Twilight Shroud does — invisibility and unselectability are different, and Riot's text says only invisible, so I did not claim it.
